newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia faces wave of poverty protests.
newsitem.headline: Croatia faces wave of poverty protests.

text.p: Croatia faced a wave of poverty protests after civil servants on Thursday announced their strike over wages, joining the ranks of disgruntled pensioners and workers.

Dissatisfied by a failure by government to raise their salaries, university teachers and employees of research institutes in capital Zagreb are to stage a three-hour strike on November 27, according to state news agency Hina.
Meanwhile, pensioners, oppressed by plunging living standards, set their protest for Saturday to demand a 40-percent increase in a meagre monthly income of some $150.
Railmen also threatened to go on a general strike next week over the future of indebted Croatian Railways after the government said it would slash its subsidy next year.
This comes only a month after metal and wood-processing workers in the port town of Rijeka protested as their industries slipped, threatening layoffs.
Croatian government has drafted a budget envisaging larger welfare expenditures in 1997 to improve the crumbling social structure after three years of an economic austerity drive.
